name: Mango Lassi
tip: Skip the honey if the mango is very ripe.

name: Acai Berry Blend
tip: Use less milk and eat it with a spoon for a bowl.

name: Apricot Orange
tip: Soak the apricots in warm water for five minutes if they are very dry.

name: Mango Chili Cooler
tip: Start with a sliver of jalapeño, taste, then add more.

name: Mango Turmeric
tip: The pinch of black pepper is what makes turmeric absorbable.

name: Green Peanut Butter Cup
tip: The cocoa hides the color if greens are a hard sell.

name: Zucchini Vanilla Green
tip: Frozen zucchini makes it creamy without tasting like vegetables.

name: Sweet Green Starter
tip: A mild first green smoothie — mostly fruit, one cup of spinach.

name: Tart Cherry Recovery
tip: Tart cherry is a classic post-training choice for sore legs.

name: Egg White Vanilla Shake
tip: Use pasteurized egg whites only.

name: Big Build Shake
tip: High calorie by design — this is the one for a bulking phase.

name: Bedtime Casein
tip: Casein digests slowly, which is the point before bed.

name: Chia Breakfast Blend
tip: Let it sit two minutes after blending and the chia thickens it.

name: Sunflower Seed Breakfast
tip: Nut-free, so it works for school-safe mornings.

name: Chocolate Avocado Mousse
tip: Thick by design. Chill it and eat it with a spoon.

name: Frozen Peach Bellini
tip: Add the prosecco last and pulse briefly so it keeps some fizz.

name: Monster Smoothie
tip: Call it a monster and the spinach stops being a problem.

name: Fiber Fix
tip: Drink it soon after blending — psyllium thickens fast.

name: Iron Boost Green
tip: Vitamin C from the orange helps you absorb the iron from the greens.

name: Chilled Gazpacho
tip: Chill it an hour before serving.

name: Blender Basil Pesto
tip: Pulse rather than run it long if you want texture.

name: Steel Cut Sunday
tip: Cooked steel-cut oats blend cleanest straight from the fridge — warm ones turn gluey under the blade.

name: The Mill Shake
tip: Oat flour hydrates instantly, so pour it over the milk and give it a minute before the blade runs or you get a paste ring on the wall.

name: Pear and Bran Wake-Up
tip: Leave the pear skin on — it is most of the fibre and it disappears completely at this ratio.

name: Swiss Muesli Cup
tip: Let the muesli soak in the milk for a full minute first — the dried fruit in it is what jams a dry blade.

name: Trail Mix Morning
tip: Use a clustery granola rather than a loose one; the clusters break into flecks you can still feel, which is the point.

name: Turkish Oat Cup
tip: Brew the espresso ahead and chill it — hot coffee on oats makes porridge before the lid is even on.

name: Black Currant Porridge Cup
tip: Black currants are sharper than they look; taste before you add the second spoon of honey.

name: Bircher Classic
tip: The original is grated apple soaked overnight — if you have the night, soak the oats in the juice and this blends in ten seconds.

name: Alpine Bircher
tip: Hazelnut butter separates in the jar; stir it properly before you spoon it in or you get a slick of oil on top.

name: Overnight Vanilla Jar
tip: Oats and chia both want the liquid first — add them to the milk, count to sixty, then blend.

name: Overnight Cocoa Jar
tip: The pinch of salt is not optional with cacao — without it the whole thing tastes flat and chalky.

name: Lunchbox Jar
tip: Use a seedy jam rather than jelly — the seeds survive the blade and give it something to be.

name: Andes Morning
tip: Rinse and cool the quinoa properly — any leftover saponin reads as soap in a cold drink.

name: Buckwheat Blini Shake
tip: Buttermilk plus buckwheat is a tang-on-tang build; the honey is doing real work, don't cut it.

name: Millet and Honey Morning
tip: Soak the dried apricots in a splash of hot water for a minute so they blend instead of bouncing.

name: Alegria Morning
tip: Named for the Mexican amaranth bar — if you can find popped amaranth, a spoonful on top keeps the crunch.

name: Highland Teff Shake
tip: Teff carries a faint cocoa note of its own, so go easy on anything you add for sweetness until you taste it.

name: Horchata Morning Rice
tip: Soak the almonds in hot water ten minutes and the skins slip off — that is the difference between silky and gritty.

name: Golden Apricot Wheat
tip: Wheat germ goes rancid quickly — keep the jar in the freezer and smell it before it goes in.

name: Vanilla Chia Set
tip: Chia needs to go in with the liquid and sit a minute or it clumps on the blade in a single grey knot.

name: Mango Chia Cup
tip: Frozen mango chills the mix before the chia has swelled, so give the seeds their minute in the coconut milk first.

name: Cinnamon Flax Morning
tip: Buy flaxseed whole and grind it as you need it; pre-ground flax loses its nuttiness within weeks of opening.

name: Raspberry Lime Chia
tip: Zest the lime before you juice anything — zest off a squeezed half is a miserable job.

name: Soft Pear Morning
tip: Psyllium thickens in under a minute and keeps going — drink this one soon after it is made or it sets in the cup.

name: Blackberry Flax Rise
tip: Blackberry seeds never fully break down — lean into it, or swap to blueberries if that bothers you.

name: Bottom of the Bowl
tip: This is the sweet milk left at the end of the bowl, on purpose — let the flakes go soft in the milk before blending.

name: Crispy Treat Morning
tip: Add half the cereal at the start and the rest after ten seconds of blending, so some of it stays gritty.

name: Cereal Milk Cup
tip: Toast the cornflakes on a tray for five minutes first if you want the version that tastes like the ice cream shop.

name: Cinnamon Roll Morning
tip: The cream cheese is the icing — it has to be soft or it stays in pale specks.

name: Bakery Loaf Cup
tip: The blacker the banana before it went in the freezer, the closer this gets to the loaf.

name: Frosted Carrot Morning
tip: Grate the carrot rather than chunking it — the Blast will chew chunks, but you will find orange threads in the last mouthful.

name: Streusel Apple Morning
tip: Use two different apples if you have them — one sharp, one sweet — which is what a good pie does anyway.

name: Autumn Spice Bran
tip: Canned pumpkin, not pie filling — the filling is already sugared and will take the drink somewhere sickly.

name: Muffin Basket Morning
tip: Lemon zest is what makes a blueberry muffin taste like a blueberry muffin rather than just blueberries.

name: French Toast Tuesday
tip: Only pasteurized whites belong in a cold drink — check the carton says so before you pour.

name: Short Stack Shake
tip: Yesterday's leftover pancakes work better than fresh ones; a little staleness keeps them from turning to glue.

name: Toast and Peanut Morning
tip: Toast the oats first and this stops being oatmeal and starts being toast.

name: Buttered Toast and Jam
tip: Salted butter, and only a teaspoon — any more and it beads on the surface as it warms up.

name: Almond Croissant Morning
tip: Almond extract is ferocious — a quarter teaspoon is already at the edge, and half will taste like marzipan gone wrong.

name: Crumb Coffee Cake Cup
tip: Sour cream is what makes a coffee cake tender, and it does the same thing here — yogurt is not the same swap.

name: Lemon Poppy Seed Loaf
tip: Add the poppy seeds at the very end and pulse once — blending them fully turns the whole cup a dull grey.

name: Egg White Oat Builder
tip: Pasteurized whites blend to a foam head — let it stand thirty seconds and the foam settles back in.

name: Skyr Oat Morning
tip: Skyr is thick enough to stall the blade on its own, so it goes in after the milk, never first.

name: Cottage Crunch Morning
tip: Blend the cottage cheese with the milk alone for ten seconds first — that is what kills the curds.

name: Quark and Berry Morning
tip: Quark is milder and less sour than Greek yogurt, so it takes fruit that would otherwise need sweetening.

name: Kefir Bircher Cup
tip: Let the oats sit in the kefir a minute before blending; it is thick, so they hydrate slower than they would in milk.

name: Labneh and Date Morning
tip: Labneh, dates and tahini is a Levantine breakfast plate — a pinch of salt makes all three louder.

name: Slow Build Oat
tip: Casein thickens as it sits, so if you are drinking this at your desk in twenty minutes, add another splash of milk now.

name: Avocado Oat Morning
tip: A half avocado is the limit before this stops being a drink and starts being a dip.

name: Green Builder Morning
tip: Frozen avocado gives you cold and creamy in one ingredient, so you do not need ice watering it down.

name: Savory Tomato Oat Cup
tip: Closer to salmorejo than to porridge — the oats are doing the job the stale bread does there.

name: Miso Morning Oat
tip: White miso only, and keep the broth cool — heat past a simmer flattens miso into plain salt.

name: Sweet Potato Tahini Morning
tip: Roast the sweet potato rather than boiling it — boiled, it brings water and no sweetness.

name: Matcha Avocado Morning
tip: Sift the matcha or rub it through your fingers on the way in; it clumps into bitter green pellets otherwise.

name: Savoury Chickpea Morning
tip: Peel the chickpeas if you have five spare minutes — the skins are the only thing standing between this and smooth.

name: Two Minute Oat
tip: Pour the milk, tip the oats in, find your keys, then blend — the minute they sit is what makes it smooth.

name: Grab the Granola
tip: Pitted dates or you will hear about it — check each one, even the bags that claim to be pitted.

name: Desk Drawer Chia
tip: Powdered peanut butter is the trick for a desk drawer — it will not go rancid and it thickens as the chia sets.

name: Ten Past Eight
tip: A ripe pear needs no sweetener here; a hard one needs a teaspoon of honey.

name: Cold Brew Oat Run
tip: Cold brew concentrate is roughly three times the strength of drip — a quarter cup is a full coffee's worth.

name: Goji Millet Gold
tip: Soak the goji berries five minutes or they stay leathery — the soaking water goes in too.

name: Fresa Brava
tip: Wet the rim with a spent lime shell and roll it in Tajín before you blend, not after — the glass has to be dry-handed or the seasoning slides off.

name: Golden Hour Margarita
tip: Taste it before you pour: anything this cold reads about a third less sweet than it did at room temperature, so a frozen margarita wants more agave than a shaken one.

name: Dusk in Oaxaca
tip: Date syrup stands in for tamarind here — sticky, dark and a little sour, so hold back on other sweeteners until you've tasted.

name: Sandía Ahumada
tip: Watermelon is mostly water, so it freezes hard and thins fast — keep the added ice low or you'll end up with pink slush that tastes of nothing.

name: Desert Bloom
tip: Peel prickly pear with a fork and a knife, never your fingers — the glochids are invisible and they sit in the skin.

name: Cool Heat Margarita
tip: Scrape the seeds and white ribs out of the jalapeño — that's where the burn lives, and the green pepper flavour you actually want is in the flesh.

name: Smoke and Serrano
tip: Serrano is sharper and faster than jalapeño; start with half and blend for five seconds less than you think, because heat keeps climbing as it sits.

name: Laguna Azul
tip: Frozen limeade concentrate is sour and sweet in one spoon, which is why bars keep it around for slush drinks — no separate syrup needed.

name: Havana Lime Freeze
tip: Three ingredients means nowhere to hide — squeeze the lime to order, since bottled juice tastes cooked and the whole drink rests on it.

name: Golden Banana Freeze
tip: Brown sugar rather than white — the molasses edge is what makes a banana daiquiri taste like rum instead of milkshake.

name: Papa Doble Freeze
tip: Cut the white pith off the grapefruit segments before they go in; blended pith turns bitter in a way no amount of syrup fixes.

name: Tortola Painkiller
tip: Grate the nutmeg over the top after pouring rather than blending it in — the aroma is half the drink and it dies under the blade.

name: Toasted Colada
tip: Toast the shredded coconut dry in a pan until it just colours, then let it cool — warm coconut will loosen the whole blend.

name: Lava Flow
tip: For the striped look, blend the strawberry alone first, spoon it into the glass, then blend the colada side and pour it down the middle.

name: Mojito Negro
tip: Clap the mint between your palms before it goes in; shredding it on the blade for too long turns it grassy and grey.

name: Paloma Rosada
tip: Brew the hibiscus double strength and chill it — hot tea poured over ice in the cup melts your texture before the blade even turns.

name: Humo y Toronja
tip: A pinch of salt on the rim does more for grapefruit than sugar does — it pushes the bitterness back and lets the fruit through.

name: Venetian Freeze
tip: Blend everything but the prosecco, then stir the prosecco in at the top of the cup — blending it flat wastes the only bubbles in the drink.

name: Rossini Freeze
tip: Same rule as a Bellini: the wine goes in last, folded through with a spoon, never spun on the blade.

name: Sunday Mimosa Freeze
tip: Zest the orange before you juice it — a spoon of zest is what separates this from orange juice with wine in it.

name: Aperol Sunset Slush
tip: Aperol is bitter-sweet already, so this needs no syrup at all — it needs acid, which is why the orange should be fresh rather than from a carton.

name: Campari Sorbetto
tip: Let the sorbet sit out two minutes before blending; rock-hard sorbet makes the blade cavitate and you'll be stirring the cup instead of drinking.

name: Frosé Hour
tip: Freeze the rosé in an ice tray the night before and use those cubes in place of half the plain ice — it's the only way frosé doesn't taste watered.

name: Red Sangria Slush
tip: Use a young, fruity red — anything oaky turns bitter and dusty once it's frozen and sweetened.

name: Kalimotxo Slush
tip: Let the cola go flat on purpose first; blending fizzy cola builds pressure under the lid and foams over the moment you open it.

name: Orchard Sangria Slush
tip: A splash of dry vermouth gives a white sangria the herbal backbone that fruit juice alone never gets to.

name: Midnight Oil
tip: Freeze leftover espresso into a tray and use those cubes — coffee ice keeps it cold without diluting the coffee, which plain ice always does.

name: Dublin Fog
tip: Blend the coffee and whiskey first, then pulse the cream in for two seconds only — over-blended cream stiffens and you lose the float.

name: Café Bandido
tip: Reposado works better than blanco here — the barrel sweetness meets the coffee halfway instead of fighting it.

name: Bushwacker
tip: This is a Gulf Coast beach drink and it lives or dies on thickness — if it pours rather than slumps, add ice cream, not more ice.

name: Grasshopper Freeze
tip: Green crème de menthe colours it, white keeps it pale — the flavour is identical, so pick by the glass you're pouring into.

name: Chocolate Monkey
tip: A pinch of salt in anything chocolate — it doesn't make the drink salty, it makes the cocoa taste like cocoa.

name: Caipirinha Freeze
tip: Quarter the lime and cut out the white core before it goes in whole — that core is the bitter part, and a blender finds it instantly.

name: Caipifruta Maracujá
tip: Leave some of the passion fruit seeds in and pulse rather than blend — the crunch is the point in Brazil, not a flaw.

name: Pisco Sour Freeze
tip: Run it ten seconds longer than feels necessary — the egg white needs the extra time to build the foam cap that makes it a sour.

name: Lúcuma Pisco Freeze
tip: Lúcuma powder tastes like maple and sweet potato and it's very absorbent — add it last so it doesn't cake on the bottom of the cup.

name: Michelada Frappé
tip: Pour the beer down the side of the cup and blend on the shortest run you can — the foam wants to climb, and a light lager gives you the most room.

name: Beerita Freeze
tip: Let the beer sit open for ten minutes first; flat beer blends cleanly and the drink doesn't lose half its volume to foam.

name: Garden Mary Freeze
tip: Blending the celery in rather than using it as a stirrer gives you the vegetal note all the way through instead of only at the first sip.

name: Jamaica Rosa
tip: Steep hibiscus cold overnight instead of boiling it — hot water pulls out a tannic edge that fights the gin.

name: Elderflower Hedgerow
tip: Peel the cucumber if the skin is waxed; the wax is bitter and blending drives it through the whole drink.

name: Sorrel Freeze
tip: Cloves go a long way — a quarter spoon is the whole Caribbean Christmas note, and double that tastes like a cough drop.

name: Sgroppino Freeze
tip: Venetians serve this between courses, which is why it stays sharp — resist the urge to sweeten it, and fold the prosecco in off the blade.

name: Amalfi Blue
tip: Keep the limoncello in the freezer — it won't solidify, and starting it that cold means less ice is needed to set the drink.

name: Negroni Frappé
tip: Frozen bitterness lands harder than stirred, so the splash of orange juice isn't a shortcut — it's what keeps this drinkable at slush temperature.

name: Juniper Slush
tip: Blend the tonic in with everything else and accept it goes flat — quinine is what you're after here, not the fizz.

name: Melon Ball Freeze
tip: Freeze the honeydew cubes first — fresh melon is so watery that it blends to soup unless it comes in cold and hard.

name: French Martini Freeze
tip: The foam on top comes from the pineapple juice, so use the kind with pulp and don't let it sit before you pour.

name: Lychee Sake Slush
tip: Pit the lychees properly — the stones are slippery and hard enough to mark a blade.

name: Watermelon Soju Slush
tip: In Korea this gets served in the hollowed-out melon; in a Blast cup, the move is to keep it barely sweet so the fruit reads clean.

name: Peach Porch Bourbon
tip: Warm the honey with a spoon of hot water before it goes in, or it hits the cold peaches and seizes into a lump.

name: Whiskey Sour Freeze
tip: Two parts sour to one part sweet is the ratio to hold onto — then nudge the syrup up a touch because the cold flattens it.

name: Bluegrass Julep Freeze
tip: A julep is supposed to be crushed ice and nothing else, so this one wants the full ice load — frost on the outside of the cup means you got it right.

name: Dark and Stormy Freeze
tip: A knob of fresh ginger alongside the ginger beer puts the heat back that blending takes out.

name: Bourbon Street Hurricane
tip: Hold back the grenadine and drizzle it in after pouring — it sinks and gives you the sunset the drink is named for.

name: Spiced Pear Freeze
tip: Use a pear that gives slightly at the neck; a firm one blends to grit and tastes of nothing at all.

name: Guava Bandera
tip: Guava nectar is already sweetened, so the lime here is doing structural work — don't cut it back.

name: Crimson Cooler
tip: Raw cranberries are aggressively sour, so this needs roughly twice the syrup you'd use with any other berry.

name: Cherry Amaretto Chill
tip: Amaretto and cherry stone are the same almond note, which is why this tastes like one ingredient rather than two.

name: Blood Orange Fizz Freeze
tip: Blood oranges fade to brown once cut, so segment them straight into the cup and blend right away to keep the colour.

name: Athens Frappé
tip: Greek frappé is foam first — give the instant coffee, sugar and a splash of the water ten seconds on their own before the ice and milk join them.

name: Saigon Ice
tip: Frozen coffee cubes instead of plain ice are what keep this from melting into brown water halfway down the cup.

name: Brown Sugar Shakerato
tip: Barista oat milk is formulated not to split against espresso — the regular kind can curdle at the edges.

name: Café de Olla Freeze
tip: Molasses stands in for piloncillo here; a full tablespoon tastes assertive warm and lands about right once it is frozen.

name: Cardamom Turkish Freeze
tip: Cardamom belongs in with the coffee rather than sprinkled on top — it needs the liquid to open up.

name: Horchata con Café
tip: Rice milk is thin, so the cinnamon carries the body here — use more than feels sensible.

name: Midnight Mocktini
tip: The crema is the whole point, so pull the espresso straight into the cup and blend it while it is still fresh.

name: Dutch Process Mocha
tip: Dutch cocoa is alkalised, so it reads rounder and darker than natural cacao and needs less sugar to stop it tasting sharp.

name: Seventy Percent Mocha
tip: Salt is not optional in anything chocolate — a quarter teaspoon is the difference between bitter and deep.

name: Oaxaca Mocha
tip: Cayenne and cacao are an old pairing — the heat should arrive after the chocolate, not with it, so keep it to a scant quarter teaspoon.

name: Deep Cocoa Cup
tip: Espresso powder deepens a chocolate drink without tasting of coffee; half a teaspoon does it, a whole one tips it into mocha.

name: Ghee Coffee Ritual
tip: Fat coffee has to be blended rather than stirred — run the full cycle or it separates into a slick before you finish the cup.

name: MCT Cold Start
tip: Start MCT oil at a teaspoon and work up; a full tablespoon on an empty stomach is a lot the first time.

name: Keto Cocoa Espresso
tip: Erythritol reads cold on the tongue, which suits a frozen drink and would taste strange in the same recipe served hot.

name: Dalgona Cloud
tip: Only instant coffee whips — brewed coffee and espresso will never build that foam, however long you run the blade.

name: Snowcap Matcha
tip: Matcha clumps unless it meets liquid first — wet it with the water at the bottom of the cup before the milk and ice go in.

name: Nocciola Affogato
tip: Add the espresso last and blend in short bursts; long blending melts the gelato and you lose the thickness that makes it an affogato.

name: Olive Oil Affogato
tip: Use a grassy, peppery olive oil rather than a mild one — with vanilla and salt it reads as savoury caramel.

name: Burnt Sugar Cold Brew
tip: Lucuma tastes like caramel left in the sun; it stretches the caramel sauce so you can use less of it.

name: Tahini Halva Coffee
tip: Stir the tahini jar down to the bottom first — the separated oil on top is what makes it blend smooth instead of gritty.

name: Pistachio Rose Latte
tip: Rose water goes from perfume to soap in about half a teaspoon, so measure it rather than pouring.

name: Bangkok Street Tea
tip: Brew the tea at double strength and chill it first — a cup of ice dilutes everything by roughly half.

name: Masala Chai Chill
tip: Fresh ginger and extra cardamom wake up bottled chai concentrate, which is usually sweet and shy on spice.

name: Bergamot Fog
tip: Orange zest stands in for the bergamot in Earl Grey — take only the coloured skin, the white pith under it is bitter.

name: Roast House Tea Latte
tip: Toast the sesame in a dry pan for a minute first; that roasted edge is what makes this taste like hōjicha rather than plain tea.

name: Sencha Citrus Snow
tip: Brew the green tea just off the boil and no longer than two minutes — scalded tea turns bitter, and cold makes that worse.

name: Sorrel Cold Brew
tip: Hibiscus is tart enough to read as fruit, so this needs far less sweetener than any milk-based coffee.

name: Mate Verde Lift
tip: Slap the mint between your palms before it goes in — bruising releases the oil, while shredding it on the blade just tastes green.

name: Mate Cacao Charge
tip: Maca is malty and faintly bitter; the cacao and banana are what make it taste deliberate rather than like a supplement.

name: Chamomile Decaf Cream
tip: Chamomile turns bitter past about five minutes of steeping, and that bitterness stacks with the coffee.

name: Black Velvet Cold Brew
tip: Cold brew is far less acidic than drip, so it takes sweetener differently — start at half what you would use in iced drip, then taste.

name: Peppermint Espresso Frost
tip: Peppermint extract is brutal by volume: a quarter teaspoon flavours the whole cup, half a teaspoon tastes like toothpaste.

name: Cold Brew Vanilla Lift
tip: Freeze whatever coffee is left in the pot in an ice tray — those cubes are the single best upgrade to any blended iced coffee.

name: Doppio Power Shake
tip: Let the espresso sit a minute before it meets the whey; near-boiling liquid makes the protein seize into lumps.

name: Velvet Cottage Coffee
tip: Cottage cheese only goes properly smooth if it starts with the liquid and runs the whole cycle; stop early and it stays grainy.

name: Cold Brew Peanut Bar
tip: Powdered peanut butter carries the flavour with a fraction of the oil, so the shake stays drinkable instead of claggy.

name: Cinnamon Cold Brew Oats
tip: Soak the oats in the cold brew for five minutes before you blend and the texture goes from sandy to creamy.

name: Matcha Chia Start
tip: Add the chia at the end and give it two minutes before drinking — straight in, it clumps around the blade.

name: Espresso Meringue Shake
tip: Use pasteurised whites from a carton rather than a shell egg, and run it long enough to build the foam on top.

name: Tofu Mocha Silk
tip: Silken tofu is the dairy-free route to milkshake texture; drain the packing water or the drink tastes faintly of the box.

name: Rooibos Vanilla Wind-Down
tip: Rooibos carries no caffeine at all, which makes it the one tea base that still works as a shake after dinner.

name: Late Shift Decaf
tip: Casein keeps thickening as it stands, so drink it within a few minutes or blend it looser than you think you want.

name: Soda Fountain Classic
tip: Half a cup of milk, not a full one — thin milkshakes are almost always a liquid problem, never an ice cream problem.

name: Pink Counter
tip: Frozen strawberries beat fresh here — fresh ones bring water, and water is what makes a pink shake taste watery.

name: Black And White
tip: Pulse rather than run it — a few short bursts leave dark ribbons through the vanilla instead of blending it all to brown.

name: Malt Shop Memory
tip: No malt powder in the house: oat flour with brown sugar lands in the same toasted, slightly savoury place.

name: Brooklyn Egg Cream
tip: Blend the milk and syrup first, then add the sparkling water and pulse once — a long blend flattens every bubble out of it.

name: Too Thick For A Straw
tip: Let the ice cream sit out four or five minutes first; rock-hard scoops just cavitate and the blade spins in an air pocket.

name: Midnight Sandwich
tip: Hold back two cookies and drop them in for the last three seconds — you want rubble, not a uniform grey shake.

name: Speculoos Drift
tip: Speculoos are already cinnamon-heavy, so resist adding more spice; the frozen banana is doing the creamy work in place of ice cream.

name: Vanilla Wafer Icebox
tip: This is the old icebox cake, so let it stand two minutes after blending — the wafers soften and the texture stops being sandy.

name: Corner Piece Brownie
tip: A teaspoon of espresso powder doesn't read as coffee; it just makes the chocolate taste darker and more like a real brownie edge.

name: Confetti Candle
tip: Almond extract is the whole trick behind boxed birthday cake flavour — half a teaspoon, no more, or it turns medicinal.

name: Campfire Graham
tip: Fluff sticks to everything — spoon it onto the ice cream rather than into the milk, so it doesn't weld itself to the bottom of the cup.

name: Deep Cup Peanut
tip: Use the salted peanut butter, not the fancy unsalted stuff; the salt is the entire reason a peanut butter cup works.

name: Salt Lick Caramel
tip: Add the salt, taste, then add a little more — caramel without salt reads as flat sweetness, and most people stop short.

name: Raspberry In White
tip: White chocolate has no cocoa solids to cut the sugar, so the raspberries and the squeeze of lemon are doing all the balancing.

name: Florida Icebox
tip: Zest the limes before you juice them — it is impossible afterwards, and the zest is where the perfume actually lives.

name: Lemon Curd Cloud
tip: Whole-milk yogurt, not nonfat — the fat is what keeps curd from tasting like sweetened lemon squash.

name: Harvest Field Pumpkin
tip: Check the tin — pumpkin pie filling is already sweetened and spiced, and stacking this on top of it is too much.

name: Pecan Pie In A Cup
tip: Toast the pecans in a dry pan for two minutes if you have them raw — untoasted pecans taste papery and vanish into the milk.

name: Carrot Cake Sundae
tip: Grate the carrot rather than chunking it; the Blast will turn shreds creamy but it leaves chunks as orange confetti.

name: Mascarpone And Coffee
tip: Freezing leftover coffee in an ice tray is the whole trick — plain ice dilutes it, coffee cubes only make it stronger.

name: Cherry On The Cheesecake
tip: The lemon juice isn't optional — cheesecake reads as cheesecake because of the acid, not because of the cheese.

name: Passion Fruit Cheesecake
tip: Passion fruit seeds crack under the blade and turn slightly bitter; scoop the pulp and leave half the seeds behind.

name: Banoffee Stack
tip: Frozen banana instead of fresh keeps this thick enough to stand a spoon in, which is the point of banoffee.

name: Tres Leches Cup
tip: A leftover pancake stands in for the sponge; tear it up and let it soak in the milks for a minute before you hit blend.

name: Beet Velvet Cake
tip: Cooked beet is where red velvet got its colour long before food dye; a quarter cup is plenty, more and it tastes like soil.

name: Sticky Toffee Pudding
tip: Soak the dates in hot water for five minutes and drain them — dry dates leave little leathery specks the blade won't catch.

name: Soft Serve, No Machine
tip: Frozen banana is the entire reason a dairy-free shake comes out creamy instead of icy — slice it before freezing or it welds into a brick.

name: Mango Lime Nice Cream
tip: Lime with mango is not a garnish — without the acid, frozen mango on its own tastes cloying about halfway down the cup.

name: Açaí Bowl In A Cup
tip: Unsweetened açaí is genuinely bitter and earthy; the dates and the banana are what turn it into a dessert rather than a chore.

name: Dark Cherry Nice Cream
tip: The spoon of almond butter is there for fat, not flavour — fat is what stops a fruit-only blend from setting up like a slushie.

name: Peanut Butter Soft Serve
tip: Start with half the oat milk and add the rest only if the blade stalls — this one should be scoopable, not pourable.

name: Field Strawberry Soft Serve
tip: A teaspoon of sea moss gel is a flavourless thickener — it holds a dairy-free blend together the way egg yolk holds custard.

name: Pineapple Whip
tip: Coconut cream, not coconut milk beverage — the thin carton stuff will not hold the swirl and you end up with pineapple juice.

name: Avocado Lime Freeze
tip: Avocado in dessert is standard across Brazil and Vietnam; it brings fat and silk, and the lime keeps it from tasting like guacamole.

name: Fig And Tahini Freeze
tip: Snip the hard stem off each dried fig first — it never breaks down and it is the one bit you'll notice.

name: Palm Grove Shake
tip: Medjool dates, not Deglet Noor — Medjools are soft enough to blend smooth and caramel enough that you need nothing else.

name: Soursop Freeze
tip: Soursop hides big black seeds in the pulp and they are bitter — pick them out by hand before anything goes near the blade.

name: Lucuma Cream
tip: Lucuma tastes like maple and sweet potato had a fruit; it is subtle, so don't bury it under cocoa or coffee.

name: Sandía Granita
tip: Freeze the watermelon in cubes the night before and you need almost no added water, which is what keeps a granita from going slushy.

name: Espresso Granita
tip: Sweeten the espresso while it is still hot so the sugar dissolves; stirred into a cold blend it stays gritty.

name: Raspberry Rose Ice
tip: Rose water goes from lovely to soap at about a teaspoon — start with half and smell the cup before you add more.

name: Sicilian Lemon Ice
tip: Sugar and acid in roughly equal spoons is the sorbet ratio; too little sugar and it freezes into a solid lump rather than a slush.

name: Drowned Gelato
tip: Pull the espresso and let it cool thirty seconds before it hits the gelato, or the first half melts to soup before the blade turns.

name: Cacao And Chilli
tip: The heat should arrive after the chocolate, not with it — a quarter teaspoon is a warm finish, half is a dare.

name: Bitter Chocolate And Sea Salt
tip: Chop the bar before it goes in; whole squares bounce off the blade and you end up with shards rather than a smooth blend.

name: Chocolate Tahini Freeze
tip: Stir the tahini jar all the way to the bottom first — the oil that sits on top is not the sesame paste you want here.

name: Halva Shake
tip: Tahini is bitter on its own and that is the point — the honey should only take the edge off, not cover it.

name: Cacao Nib Crunch
tip: Nibs are unsweetened chocolate with no sugar and no fat added back, so they stay crunchy and bitter — the dates carry the sweetness.

name: Chocolate And Olive Oil
tip: Use the peppery green olive oil you'd finish a salad with, not the neutral cooking one; that bitterness is what makes this work.

name: One Banana, Frozen
tip: This is frozen banana and nothing else, and it is genuinely good — but it is not a milkshake, and it will not pretend to be one.

name: Cookie Crumb Lite
tip: A cookies-and-cream protein powder gets you the flavour without the cookies, but it will never have the rubble — accept that or eat the real one.

name: Light Caramel Malt
tip: One teaspoon of real caramel sauce plus salt beats three teaspoons of caramel syrup, because salt is what your tongue reads as caramel.

name: Lean Chocolate Thickshake
tip: An eighth of a teaspoon of xanthan is the whole difference between a thin protein shake and one that coats the glass — any more turns it slimy.

name: Peanut Butter Lite
tip: Powdered peanut butter has most of the oil pressed out, so it tastes peanutty but blends thin — the frozen banana is carrying the body.

name: Mango Sticky Rice
tip: The salt is not optional — mango sticky rice is a salty-sweet dish, and without it this just tastes like a mango smoothie.

name: Black Sesame Freeze
tip: Toast the sesame hard, almost to the edge of burning; pale sesame gives you texture and no flavour at all.

name: Maple Pecan Nice Cream
tip: Maple extract rather than syrup keeps this thick — syrup is liquid, and liquid is the enemy of a scoopable blend.

name: Cereal Milk
tip: Let the cornflakes steep in the cold milk for five minutes before blending; that soak is the flavour, the blending is just texture.

name: Orange And Olive Oil Ice
tip: A dairy-free ice with a teaspoon of good olive oil comes out rounder and less icy, because fat is what mouthfeel is made of.

name: Training Wheels
tip: Romaine is the mildest thing in the crisper drawer — it gives you the colour and almost none of the flavour, which is the whole point on day one.

name: Soft Landing
tip: Use a pear that gives under your thumb; a hard one tastes like nothing and leaves grit on the blade.

name: Quiet Green
tip: Frozen spinach blends smoother and tastes noticeably milder than fresh — the freezing softens the leaf so there are no green flecks and no raw edge.

name: Monsoon Green
tip: The salt is not seasoning, it is a bitterness switch — leave it out once and you will taste the leaf immediately.

name: Cardamom Halva
tip: Tear the dates and drop them in first so they sit against the blade; whole pitted dates tend to ride the top of the cup.

name: Cassis Leaf
tip: Black currants are tart enough to carry the spinach on their own — taste before you reach for anything sweet.

name: Green Velvet
tip: No sweetener at all here, so the lime is doing the work — two tablespoons sounds like a lot and is exactly right.

name: Green Truffle
tip: Cacao hides frozen spinach completely — this is the one to hand someone who insists they can taste greens anywhere.

name: Kale Outvoted
tip: Strip the leaves off the ribs before they go in — the ribs are where the bitterness and the stringiness both live.

name: Sesame Grove
tip: Tahini fat coats the tongue and blunts kale's edge — it does more for the drink than another spoon of sweetener would.

name: Miso Verde
tip: Savoury and meant to be drunk cold; if the broth is fridge-cold the miso needs a second longer to disperse.

name: Kerala Green
tip: Frozen kale is milder and far smoother than fresh — no fibrous bits, so you can use it in a drink this creamy without straining.

name: Forest Floor
tip: Dark cherry and cacao want salt the way caramel does; without it the drink tastes flat and slightly chalky.

name: Orchard Green
tip: Baby kale is tender enough to skip the stem-stripping you would do with the mature leaf.

name: Pistachio Grove
tip: Pistachio butter is thick and sticky — spoon it on top of the liquid, not onto the dry blade, or it welds itself to the bottom.

name: Peppery Vine
tip: Drink this the way you would a cold soup; a ripe room-temperature tomato beats a cold one every time.

name: Clear Creek
tip: Watercress is mustardy and loud — one cup is the ceiling unless you want it to taste like horseradish.

name: Anisette Cooler
tip: Slice the fennel thin across the grain; in chunks it stays crunchy no matter how long you run the blade.

name: Cold Cress
tip: Buttermilk's acid tames the cress the way a vinaigrette tames a salad — plain milk here is dull.

name: Vineyard Cool
tip: Frozen grapes are sweet enough that this needs no sweetener and cold enough that it needs no ice.

name: Summer Bench
tip: Salted watermelon is a street-cart trick and it works just as well blended.

name: Evening Garden
tip: Brew the chamomile strong and chill it first; hot tea poured into the cup will melt the ice before the blade moves.

name: Rose Garden
tip: Rose water goes from floral to soapy in about a quarter teaspoon, so measure it rather than pouring.

name: Stained Glass
tip: Rainbow chard stems will tint the drink pink or orange — use the white-stemmed bunch if you want it to stay green.

name: Sunday Greens
tip: Collard is the toughest leaf on the list — chop it small before it goes in, or the blade just spins it around.

name: Pot Likker
tip: The splash of vinegar is what makes this taste like greens off the stove rather than a salad in a cup.

name: Hanoi Pear
tip: Use only the pale bottom third of the lemongrass stalk and smash it flat first — the upper stalk is woody and never breaks down.

name: Cold Sesame Green
tip: Toasted sesame oil is strong enough that half a teaspoon flavours the whole cup; a tablespoon would taste like salad dressing.

name: Roots and Rind
tip: Dandelion is genuinely bitter, so this one needs both the sweet and the citrus — pulling either makes it hard going.

name: Roadside Green
tip: Young dandelion leaves are far gentler than the big ragged ones; pick the small pale ones if you get the choice.

name: Crimson Stem
tip: Beet tops taste like mild chard with an earthy note, and raspberry covers that note exactly.

name: Salad Days
tip: Cottage cheese blends to a clean creaminess if you give it a full thirty seconds — stop early and you get lumps.

name: Sandwich Shop
tip: Alfalfa sprouts tangle around the blade in a clump — scatter them over the liquid rather than dropping the whole handful in.

name: Sharp Start
tip: Broccoli sprouts are peppery in a radish way — half a cup is plenty against one apple's worth of sweetness.

name: Green Spark
tip: Blend kiwi seeds briefly or not at all — run it too long and the crushed seeds turn the drink faintly bitter.

name: Cold Labneh Green
tip: Labneh is thick enough to stall the blade on its own, which is why the water goes in first and the labneh on top.

name: Little Leaf Tropical
tip: Microgreens are far more delicate than the full-grown leaf, so add them last and keep the blend short.

name: First Cut
tip: A quarter cup of wheatgrass is the whole dose — it tastes like a mown lawn at any more than that, and citrus is the only thing that covers it.

name: Agua Verde
tip: Seed the jalapeño unless you want real heat; the pith carries most of it, not the flesh.

name: Peppery Basil Cooler
tip: Bruise the basil between your palms first — whole leaves dropped in cold barely give anything up.

name: Tabbouleh Sip
tip: Flat-leaf parsley, not curly — curly parsley is tougher and tastes more like stalk than herb.

name: Cucumber Doogh
tip: Salted yogurt drinks want more salt than you think — taste it, then add another pinch.

name: Mint Condition
tip: Spearmint, not peppermint — peppermint leaves a cooling burn that fights the melon.

name: Green Apple Rebuild
tip: Pea protein has a faintly savoury edge that tart apple covers better than banana does.

name: Silken Mango Green
tip: Silken tofu, not firm — firm tofu stays in grains no matter how long the blade runs.

name: Dragon Breath
tip: Buy the pink-fleshed dragon fruit, not the white — white blends out a dull grey and the color is the entire point.

name: Mermaid Tail
tip: Half a teaspoon of blue spirulina is already vivid; go past a full one and it turns teal and tastes faintly of the sea.

name: Color-Changing Potion
tip: Blend everything except the lemon juice, then let them stir it in at the table — the acid flips butterfly pea from blue to violet while they watch.

name: Dinosaur Juice
tip: Frozen spinach blends away to nothing; fresh leaves leave green flecks that get interrogated.

name: Fairy Dust
tip: A quarter cup of cooked beet gives you the pink; half a cup starts tasting like the garden it came from.

name: Tiger Stripes
tip: Cut the carrot into coins no thicker than a penny — the Blast handles raw carrot, but only in small pieces.

name: Fireworks
tip: Blend the blueberries with the milk first and pour half out, then blend the strawberries in — you get two colors in one cup without washing anything.

name: Secret Agent Shake
tip: Use the riced cauliflower straight from the freezer — thawed, it goes watery and the cabbage taste surfaces.

name: Blast Off Chocolate
tip: Freeze zucchini already diced; a whole frozen one will not fit past the blade and you cannot cut it once it's solid.

name: Cloud Shake
tip: Rinse the beans until the water runs clear — whatever bean flavor there is lives in the canning liquid.

name: Rocket Fuel
tip: Roast the sweet potato rather than boiling it, and chill it fully — warm purée makes a sad, thick drink.

name: School Bus Shake
tip: Buzz the oats with the milk for ten seconds before anything else goes in, so nobody finds a raw flake.

name: Running Late
tip: Make it the night before and keep it in the fridge — it thickens, but a splash of milk and five seconds of BLEND brings it back.

name: Pancakes in a Straw
tip: This is what yesterday's leftover pancake is for; tear it up small so it soaks rather than spins.

name: Last of the Cornflakes
tip: Let the flakes sit in the milk for a minute before blending — they go silky instead of gritty.

name: Pajama Day Pear
tip: Brew the chamomile and chill it right down first; lukewarm is the worst temperature for a sore throat.

name: Quiet Morning Melon
tip: Peel the cucumber for this one; the skin is where any bitterness hides and today is not the day.

name: Soft Voice Apple
tip: Rooibos is naturally caffeine-free and goes sweet as it cools, so brew it strong and chill it.

name: Confetti Cup
tip: Blend it plain and let them stir the sprinkles in themselves — blended, sprinkles turn the whole cup a sad grey.

name: Candy Cane Swirl
tip: Peppermint extract is ferocious — a quarter teaspoon, measured, not a glug from the bottle.

name: Gingerbread Reindeer
tip: Molasses is strong and bitter in quantity; one teaspoon reads as gingerbread, two reads as medicine.

name: Pumpkin Patch
tip: Check the can says pure pumpkin, not pie filling — the filling is already sweetened and spiced and throws the whole thing off.

name: Snowman Shake
tip: Shredded coconut never fully disappears; if bits are a problem in your house, leave it out and add another splash of vanilla.

name: Love Bug
tip: Chop the white chocolate small or melt it into the milk first, or you'll get shards on the last sip.

name: Fluffernutter Float
tip: Spoon the fluff onto the frozen banana rather than the cup wall — it sticks to cold fruit and slides off plastic.

name: Nut-Free Lunchbox
tip: Sunflower seed butter stands in for peanut butter one-for-one, which matters if the classroom is nut-free.

name: Grape Snowstorm
tip: Freeze seedless grapes loose on a tray first, otherwise they clump into one lump that jams the blade.

name: Cutie Pie Cream
tip: Pull off every scrap of white pith — that's what turns citrus smoothies bitter as they sit.

name: Cherry Bomb
tip: Frozen dark cherries come pitted; fresh ones do not, and one missed pit will chip the blade.

name: Papaya Pup
tip: Scrape out every black seed — they're peppery and one is enough to ruin a whole cup.

name: Chocolate Chipmunk
tip: Chocolate chips go in last and get two short BLEND pulses — you want freckles, not a uniform brown.

name: Muscle Monkey
tip: One scoop is plenty at this size; two makes it chalky and no amount of banana hides it.

name: Havana Chill
tip: Blend the mint, lime and ice first and pour the sparkling water in at the end — bubbles do not survive the blade.

name: Nada-Rita
tip: Rub a cut lime around the rim and roll it in coarse salt before you pour; the rim is most of what makes it read as a margarita.

name: Isla Nada
tip: Cream of coconut is sweet and canned coconut milk is not — you need both, one for body and one for the sweetness.

name: Cuba Nada
tip: A teaspoon of date syrup gives the molasses note that rum usually brings, so the cola stops tasting like just cola.

name: Michelada Cero
tip: Without the beer you lose the carbonation, so chill the tomato juice hard and keep the ice coarse or it turns to soup.

name: Strawberry Balsamic Shrub
tip: The vinegar should read as brightness, not as vinegar — start at a teaspoon and add the last half only if the fruit tastes flat.

name: Haymaker's Switchel
tip: Grate the ginger rather than chunking it; the Blast will not fully break down a knob of fibre and you get strings in the last mouthful.

name: Blackberry Thyme Shrub
tip: Strip the thyme leaves off the stem — the woody stems never break down and they taste like twigs.

name: Orchard Shrub
tip: Leave the skin on the green apple; that is where the tannin and most of the colour live.

name: Rhubarb Sour
tip: Raw rhubarb is stringy, so slice it thin across the stalk and give it a full extra blend cycle before anything else goes in.

name: Jamaica Frost
tip: Brew the hibiscus at double strength and chill it — ice dilutes it back down to where you wanted it.

name: Hibiscus and Rosemary
tip: Rosemary goes soapy if you overdo it; one teaspoon of picked needles is the ceiling for a single cup.

name: Peach Tannin Tea
tip: Brew the tea strong and chill it first; hot tea melts the fruit and you lose the frozen texture entirely.

name: Pomegranate Black Tea
tip: Let the tea steep a minute past where you normally would — the extra tannin is what stands in for the dry edge of a wine.

name: Maghrebi Mint Freeze
tip: Green tea turns bitter if it was brewed too hot, and freezing it does not hide that — brew it at about 80C.

name: Mate Limon
tip: Mate is properly bitter and that is the point — sweeten it less than you think, then add the lemon and taste again.

name: Rooibos Amber
tip: Peel the orange but leave a strip of pith-free zest in the cup — rooibos is soft and needs the oil for lift.

name: Chamomile Gold
tip: Orange blossom water is a perfume, not a flavour — half a teaspoon perfumes the whole cup and a full one ruins it.

name: Peppermint Frost
tip: Brewed peppermint tea beats peppermint extract here; the extract tastes like toothpaste once the drink is cold.

name: Stormy Ginger Lime
tip: A teaspoon of molasses is the whole trick — it is the dark, burnt-sugar note the drink is missing.

name: Ginger Kombucha Highball
tip: Pulse rather than run it; kombucha foams hard and a long blend pushes it up past the lid.

name: Golden Ginger Spritz
tip: Fresh turmeric stains everything it touches, including the gasket — rinse the cup straight away rather than after.

name: Tepache Chill
tip: Use the core of the pineapple as well as the flesh — it is where the funk that makes this taste fermented comes from.

name: Spiced Cherry Cola
tip: Let the cola go flat on purpose before blending, then top the glass with a splash of fresh cola for the bubbles.

name: Bitter Sunset
tip: Leave a little of the white pith on the grapefruit segments — that bitterness is the whole reason this works before dinner.

name: Sevilla Spritz
tip: Marmalade rather than orange juice: the shredded peel carries the bitterness that juice alone cannot.

name: Fennel and Grapefruit
tip: Use the white bulb, not the fronds — fronds taste like dill and take the drink somewhere else entirely.

name: Basil Bitter Smash
tip: Slap the basil between your palms before it goes in; torn basil in a blender bruises black, slapped basil gives up its oil first.

name: Concord and Pepper
tip: Black pepper and grape is how you get a red-wine shape out of juice; grind it coarse so you taste it in flashes.

name: Beet and Pepper Sour
tip: Cooked beet, not raw — raw beet blends to grit and tastes like soil rather than earth.

name: Tamarindo Heat
tip: Date paste with that much lime lands close to tamarind — sticky, sour and dark — so do not cut the lime back.

name: Jicama Chili Slush
tip: Peel jicama with a knife rather than a peeler; the skin is thicker than it looks and the fibrous layer under it is what makes drinks woolly.

name: Fire and Cherry
tip: Add the cayenne in two goes and taste between them; heat in a cold drink creeps up about thirty seconds after the sip.

name: Verde Sour
tip: Scrape the seeds and white ribs out of the jalapeno — you want the green pepper flavour, not just the burn.

name: Melon y Pepino
tip: A pinch of salt is what turns melon water into a drink you would be handed at a bar rather than a glass of melon.

name: Guanabana Fresca
tip: Pick out the black seeds before blending — they are bitter and they are hard enough to mark the blade.

name: Prickly Pear Sunset
tip: Handle prickly pears with a fork and a knife, never bare hands, and halve them to scoop the flesh out of the skin.

name: Lemongrass Slush
tip: Only the pale bottom third of the stalk is tender enough to blend; slice it into coins and keep the green top for another day.

name: Rose and Lychee
tip: Rose water without acid tastes like soap; the tablespoon of lime is doing structural work, not seasoning.

name: Cardamom Pomegranate
tip: Ground cardamom fades fast in the jar — if yours smells of nothing when you open it, use more or it will not register at all.

name: Passionfruit Sour
tip: Pasteurised egg white gives you the foam cap a proper sour needs; blend it thirty seconds longer than feels necessary.

name: Raspberry Snow
tip: Blend the slush with plain water, then stir the sparkling water in by hand at the glass so it stays a fizzy slush and not a foam.

name: Starfruit Spritz
tip: Trim the brown edges off the five ridges first; they are tough and they are the bitter part.

name: Garden Tonic
tip: Cucumber and tonic is the gin shape without the gin — keep the peel on for the grassy note the botanicals usually supply.

name: Celery Salt Fizz
tip: String the celery with a peeler before it goes in, or the fibres wrap the blade and the drink never gets smooth.

name: Cactus Cooler
tip: Cactus water is much milder than coconut water, so this one needs the watermelon frozen solid or it tastes like it has been watered down.

name: Second Set
tip: Raw oats blend smoother if you soak them in the milk for five minutes first.

name: The Refill
tip: Pit the dates and tear them in half — whole ones ride on top of the blade.

name: Cooldown Cherry
tip: Unflavored whey lets the cherry stay tart; vanilla whey would flatten it out.

name: Finisher Mocha
tip: The salt is not optional — it is what makes the chocolate read as chocolate.

name: Rebuild Mango
tip: Frozen mango beats fresh here — fresh mango thins the yogurt out within the minute.

name: Heavy Set Chocolate
tip: Cacao powder on top of chocolate whey is what turns it from sweet to dark.

name: Pineapple Reload
tip: Fresh pineapple will thin dairy out over an hour, so drink this one straight away.

name: Honeycomb Oats
tip: Use a banana with brown freckles; a green one tastes starchy against the honey.

name: Featherweight Vanilla
tip: Isolate foams badly if you run it long — thirty seconds on BLEND is plenty.

name: Snow Day Strawberry
tip: Zest, not juice — the oil in the peel carries strawberry further than acid does.

name: Raspberry Frost
tip: A quarter teaspoon of xanthan is the whole trick: more and it turns to slime.

name: Quiet Peach
tip: Ground ginger, not fresh — fresh ginger fights the peach instead of backing it.

name: Blue Hour
tip: Skyr is stiffer than Greek yogurt, so pour the milk in first or it bridges the blade.

name: Blank Page
tip: Buy pasteurized whites in a carton — this is not the place for a raw egg.

name: Lights Out Vanilla
tip: Casein thickens for about a minute after it stops, so blend it looser than you want it.

name: Deep Cocoa
tip: Add the chia at the end and give it two minutes, or it clumps against the blade.

name: Ten O'Clock Pudding
tip: Leave it in the fridge twenty minutes and it sets thick enough to eat with a spoon.

name: Night Shift Cherry
tip: Brew the chamomile double strength and chill it, or the cherry buries it completely.

name: Cassis Nightcap
tip: Black currants are sharper than blackberries — taste before you add a second spoon of honey.

name: Desk Drawer Cold Brew
tip: Collagen dissolves in cold liquid without foaming, so it goes in before the ice.

name: Morning Pour
tip: Pull the espresso over ice first — hot coffee poured onto skyr will split it.

name: Istanbul Morning
tip: Cardamom in the coffee is the Turkish habit; a quarter teaspoon is already loud.

name: Salted Honey Espresso
tip: Blend the cottage cheese with the milk alone for ten seconds first so no curds survive.

name: Crumb and Cream
tip: Save half the cookie and crush it on top — blending it all in just makes grey shake.

name: Buckeye Shake
tip: Powdered peanut butter carries the flavour at a fifth of the fat of the real jar.

name: Sunday Morning Swirl
tip: Quark is the sour-cream tang that makes this taste of frosting rather than of cinnamon toast.

name: Confetti Shake
tip: Almond extract is the whole birthday-cake illusion — vanilla alone never gets there.

name: Venetian Nightcap
tip: Two tablespoons of mascarpone is enough for the whole cup to taste rich; four turns it greasy.

name: Porch Light Banana
tip: Grate the nutmeg over the top at the end; blended in, it just tastes dusty.

name: Burnt Sugar and Salt
tip: Salt the caramel in the cup before blending so it dissolves instead of sitting in grains.

name: After Dinner Mint
tip: Nibs stay crunchy where chocolate chips melt into streaks — pulse them in at the end.

name: Strawberry Crust
tip: Cottage cheese is what gives the cheesecake tang; blend it until you cannot see a single curd.

name: Fudge Pop
tip: A quarter of an avocado reads as fudge, not as avocado, as long as the cacao is unsweetened.

name: Orchard Skyr
tip: Leave the apple skin on — it is where the tartness lives, and the Blast handles it.

name: Rhubarb Whip
tip: Chop the rhubarb small and cold; long stalks wind around the blade instead of breaking down.

name: Black Mission Cream
tip: Orange blossom water is potent — half a teaspoon perfumes the whole cup, a full one soaps it.

name: Doogh Recovery
tip: Doogh is salted, not sweet — if it tastes odd, it needs more salt rather than less.

name: Bastani Shake
tip: Rose and pistachio need each other; rose on its own tastes like hand cream.

name: Bloody Build
tip: Unflavored whey is the only powder that survives a savoury build — vanilla would ruin it.

name: Buttermilk Field
tip: Buttermilk already carries acid, so go easy on the lemon or the greens turn bitter.

name: Mid-August
tip: Salted watermelon is a summer trick, not a mistake — the pinch makes it taste sweeter.

name: Late Bramble
tip: Buttermilk is thinner than yogurt but twice as tangy — it suits blackberry better.

name: Guayaba Crema
tip: Guava and cream cheese is the pastry pairing from every Cuban bakery, cold and drinkable.

name: Long Winter
tip: Two scoops is a lot of powder for one cup — add the milk first or it packs under the blade.

name: Double Scoop Morning
tip: If it is too thick to pour, top with milk and pulse twice rather than blending longer.

name: Concrete Mixer
tip: Casein and whey together give you a shake that is thick now and still filling in two hours.

name: Offseason Vanilla
tip: Granola goes in last and gets two pulses, so you keep some grit instead of sweet sludge.

name: Golden Hour Cashew
tip: Cashew butter is sweeter and softer than almond — it blends in without leaving flecks.

name: Ricotta Cloud
tip: Whole-milk ricotta blends creamy where part-skim stays grainy no matter how long you run it.

name: Winter Nog
tip: Pasteurized whites whip up airy in the Blast, which is what makes this taste like nog.

name: Halva Hour
tip: The sesame fat and the pinch of salt are what bury the chalky edge of plant protein — leave either out and you taste the powder.

name: Horchata Lift
tip: Soak the almonds in hot water for ten minutes first; they break down far smoother and you avoid the gritty bits at the bottom.

name: Bangkok Iced Tea
tip: Brew the tea at double strength and chill it — normal-strength tea disappears completely behind a scoop of protein.

name: Cardamom Chai Builder
tip: Ground cardamom loses its oils fast, so crush green pods yourself if you have them and use a scant quarter teaspoon.

name: Turkish Coffee Cacao
tip: Let the espresso cool before it goes in — hot liquid makes plant protein foam up and climb the cup.

name: Street Corn Recovery
tip: Blend the corn with the lime juice first for twenty seconds — the kernel skins need the head start or they stay as specks.

name: Miso Caramel Cloud
tip: White miso plus date syrup reads as salted caramel — but drain the tofu's packing water or the whole thing goes thin and beany.

name: Toasted Sesame Silk
tip: Toast the sesame in a dry pan until it smells nutty and let it cool — raw seeds taste flat and never bring the roasted note.

name: Butterfly Blue Cloud
tip: Butterfly pea powder is colour, not flavour; the coconut butter is what carries it, so warm the jar in your hands if it has set hard.

name: Pistachio Matcha Cloud
tip: Soy isolate is the most neutral of the plant powders, which is the only reason the matcha still comes through here.

name: Night Shift Crush
tip: Add the nibs at the end and give it one short pulse if you want the crunch to survive the crush program.

name: Mole Noir
tip: Cayenne with cacao is an old pairing — start at a quarter teaspoon, because the heat keeps building for a minute after you taste it.

name: Chili Lime Mango Lift
tip: Pea protein is the bitterest of the bunch; a full tablespoon of lime juice is doing real work here, not just seasoning.

name: Guava Silk
tip: No powder in this one at all — silken tofu and hemp hearts do it, and the lime keeps the guava from turning cloying.

name: Soursop and Hemp
tip: Hemp protein is earthy and green-tasting on its own; soursop's sourness is one of the few fruits strong enough to cover it.

name: Lychee Rose Silk
tip: Rose water goes from perfume to soap in about a quarter teaspoon, so measure it rather than pouring from the bottle.

name: Persimmon Tahini Oats
tip: Use a Fuyu persimmon you can slice like an apple; an underripe Hachiya will leave your mouth feeling stripped.

name: Sticky Fig Cardamom
tip: Snip the hard stems off the figs and soak them five minutes in hot water — dry figs bounce around the blade and stay in chunks.

name: Prickly Pear Rebuild
tip: Prickly pear seeds are hard as gravel and the Blast won't beat them, so scoop the flesh and press it through a fork first.

name: Sorrel Hibiscus Cooler
tip: Brew the hibiscus strong and cold-steep it overnight if you can — boiled hibiscus goes flat and slightly stewed.

name: Black Currant Fix
tip: Black currants are sharper than they look; taste before you add the second spoon of maple, not after.

name: Date and Espresso Oats
tip: Pit the dates and tear them in half before they go in; a whole Medjool will jam under the blade every time.

name: Peanut Ginger Crush
tip: Powdered peanut butter needs a full thirty seconds to hydrate or it sits in dry pockets — blend, wait, blend again.

name: Iron Mocha
tip: Firm tofu is dense enough to stall the blade, so cube it small and give this a longer run than you think it needs.

name: Edamame Mint Cooler
tip: Buy the edamame already shelled and run it from frozen — thawed beans go mealy and the drink loses its colour.

name: White Bean Vanilla Cream
tip: Rinse canned white beans until the water runs clear; the starchy tin liquid is the entire reason people think beans taste wrong in a shake.

name: Chickpea Cookie Dough
tip: Slip the skins off the chickpeas between your fingers — it takes two minutes and is the difference between creamy and grainy.

name: Black Bean Brownie Blend
tip: Dutch-process cocoa is less acidic than natural, which is what keeps the beans from reading as savoury.

name: Lentil Gingerbread
tip: Use well-cooked brown or red lentils, chilled — firm lentils stay as grit no matter how long you blend.

name: Golden Lentil Warmer
tip: A savoury shake needs more salt than a sweet one; taste the broth first, because low-sodium stock will leave this tasting hollow.

name: Gochujang Green Heat
tip: Gochujang is sweet as well as hot, so half a tablespoon is plenty — and trim the scallion to the white and pale green only.

name: Salmorejo Rebuild
tip: White beans stand in for the bread, so pour the olive oil in last with the blade running and it emulsifies pale pink.

name: Sweet Potato Praline
tip: Roast the sweet potato rather than boiling it and chill it overnight — boiled goes watery and takes the flavour with it.

name: Pepita Pumpkin Cup
tip: Check the tin says pure pumpkin, not pie filling — the filling is mostly sugar and will bury everything else.

name: Plantain Cacao Shake
tip: The plantain has to be black-spotted and soft; a yellow one is still starchy and tastes like raw potato.

name: Jackfruit Ginger Lift
tip: Use ripe jackfruit in syrup, drained, not the young green tin sold for pulled-pork — they are completely different foods.

name: Quinoa Blueberry Build
tip: Cold leftover quinoa is ideal here, and the lemon zest is what stops the blueberry and the powder from tasting muddy together.

name: Amaranth Atole
tip: Cooked amaranth thickens hard in the fridge, so loosen it with a splash of the soy milk before the rest goes in.

name: Apricot Lassi Build
tip: Almond yogurt is thinner than dairy yogurt, so use fresh apricots rather than tinned or the whole thing runs like juice.

name: Passion Fruit Set
tip: Passion fruit seeds blend to black flecks that some people love and some don't — strain the pulp through a fork if you're in the second camp.

name: Strawberry Rhubarb Rebuild
tip: Raw rhubarb is punishingly sour and fibrous; stew it with the maple syrup for five minutes and chill it before it goes near the cup.

name: Goji Orange Hemp
tip: Soak the goji berries in the soy milk for ten minutes first — dry ones stay leathery and catch in your teeth.

name: Acai in a Cup
tip: Unsweetened acai packs are bitter and almost savoury on their own, which is exactly why the banana isn't optional.

name: Sour Cherry Stone
tip: Check every cherry for a stone; one missed pit will chip the Blast's blade and there is no repairing it.

name: Watermelon Salt Crush
tip: Freeze watermelon in single-layer chunks on a tray, not in a bag — a frozen brick won't come apart in a portable blender.

name: Walnut Maple Silk
tip: Walnut skins carry a tannic bitterness; a thirty-second soak in hot water and a rub in a towel takes most of it off.

name: Bittersweet Espresso Whip
tip: No powder and no mascarpone — silken tofu whipped with cold espresso gets you the same texture if you blend it a full minute.

name: Banana Cacao Iron
tip: Press the firm tofu between two plates for ten minutes first; the water you squeeze out is water that would otherwise thin the shake.

name: Avocado Lime Rebuild
tip: Fat and acid together are the standard fix for a chalky powder, and half an avocado with a tablespoon of lime is the cleanest version of it.

name: Carrot Cardamom Build
tip: Cashew butter is the mildest of the nut butters, so it thickens this without arguing with the carrot.

name: Beetroot Bruiser
tip: Beet turns dull brown next to chocolate but stays vivid next to raspberry, and the lemon is what holds that colour.

name: Blue Spirulina Surf
tip: Blue spirulina is far milder than the green kind, but it stains a plastic cup — rinse straight after drinking.

name: Sea Moss Mango Build
tip: Sea moss gel thickens as it sits, so drink this one straight away or it sets to a spoonable pudding in the fridge.

name: Lucuma Maca Malt
tip: Lucuma tastes like malt and maple; maca is bitter and needs the date, so don't scale the maca up on its own.

name: Baobab Berry Snap
tip: Baobab and camu camu are both sharply sour powders — between them you need no other acid, and a whole tablespoon of camu would be undrinkable.

name: Sevilla Red
tip: Blend the tomatoes alone first so they release their juice — that liquid is what carries everything else around the blade.

name: Melon Rojo
tip: Salt the watermelon and let it sit five minutes before blending; it draws out juice and stops the soup tasting like a fruit cup.

name: Ajo Blanco
tip: Soak the almonds in hot tap water for ten minutes first — the Blast's single blade will not break down dry almonds smoothly.

name: Pepino Verde
tip: Leave the cucumber skin on for colour but scrape the seeds out, or the soup goes watery and bitter within an hour.

name: Smoked Pepper Gazpacho
tip: Jarred roasted peppers are packed in brine, so taste before you add the full half teaspoon of salt.

name: Cordoba Salmorejo
tip: Rolled oats stand in for the stale bread and thicken as they sit — blend, wait five minutes, then blend again for the proper velvet.

name: Chilled Avocado Soup
tip: Broth goes in before the avocado, always — put the fat in first and it packs under the blade and spins.

name: Tarator
tip: Pulse in short bursts so the walnuts stay a little gritty; blitzed to paste they turn the soup grey.

name: Beet and Buttermilk Chill
tip: Vacuum-packed cooked beets are the shortcut here — raw beet will not break down in this cup.

name: Golden Carrot Chill
tip: Slice the raw carrot into coins no thicker than a pencil, or you will be chewing your soup.

name: Pea and Mint Chill
tip: Let the peas thaw on the counter ten minutes; frozen-solid they behave like ice and dull the mint.

name: Chilled Corn Velvet
tip: Nutritional yeast does the work that a parmesan rind would do in a hot soup — savoury depth with no cooking.

name: Emerald Herb Dressing
tip: Capers stand in for the anchovy — they bring the same salty funk and the dressing stays vegetarian.

name: Blender Caesar
tip: This is a small pour and the blade needs something to catch — tip the cup on its side and pulse rather than running it flat.

name: Lemon Tahini Drizzle
tip: Tahini seizes into cement the moment acid hits it — keep blending past that point and the water brings it back glossy.

name: Miso Ginger Dressing
tip: White miso is already salty, so taste before reaching for the salt shaker.

name: Serrano Cilantro Vinaigrette
tip: Use the cilantro stems, not just the leaves — they carry more flavour and they break down fine in a blender.

name: Honey Dijon Shake-Up
tip: Mustard is an emulsifier, so this one holds together for days in the fridge without separating.

name: Cracked Pepper Kefir Ranch
tip: Kefir brings the tang that buttermilk would and it thickens overnight — make it thinner than you want it.

name: Peanut Lime Dressing
tip: Fish sauce is the salt here — a teaspoon disappears into the peanut and leaves only depth behind.

name: Gochujang Sesame Dressing
tip: Add the sesame seeds after the blend and stir them in, or you lose the pop of whole seed entirely.

name: Cilantro Pepita Pesto
tip: Toasted pepitas make this taste cooked without a stove — buy them roasted and salted and pull the added salt back.

name: Arugula Walnut Pesto
tip: Arugula turns bitter under a long blend, so stop as soon as it is green and grainy rather than chasing smooth.

name: Mint Pistachio Pesto
tip: Half mint, half parsley — straight mint alone reads like toothpaste on lamb or peas.

name: Almond Romesco
tip: This is thick enough to stall the blade: run it, stop, shake the cup hard, run it again until it moves on its own.

name: Green Table Salsa
tip: Pull the ribs and seeds from the jalapeno if you want the flavour without the burn — the heat lives there, not in the flesh.

name: Fire-Roasted Table Salsa
tip: Pulse, do not blend — a held button turns salsa into pink foam in about four seconds.

name: Harissa Honey Drizzle
tip: A teaspoon of honey does not make this sweet, it just rounds off harissa's sharp edge.

name: Parsley Chimichurri
tip: Chimichurri wants texture, so give it three one-second pulses and let it rest half an hour instead of blending it smooth.

name: Red Enchilada Sauce
tip: Blended cold it tastes raw and dusty; the oil and the chili powder only bloom once it hits a hot pan or a hot tray of enchiladas.

name: Soy Citrus Marinade
tip: Citrus this acidic starts breaking the surface of fish down fast — thirty minutes is plenty, overnight is too long.

name: Mojo Garlic Marinade
tip: A full tablespoon of garlic sounds like a lot until you remember it is going on pork shoulder, not into a salad.

name: Lemon Garlic Hummus
tip: Whip the tahini, lemon and water into a pale cream before the chickpeas go anywhere near the cup — that order is the whole trick.

name: Roasted Pepper Hummus
tip: Pat the peppers dry first or the brine they are packed in thins this into a sauce.

name: Green Herb Hummus
tip: It will look drab straight after blending and turn properly green about a minute later as the spinach breaks down.

name: White Bean and Olive Spread
tip: The olives carry all the salt this needs, so taste before you add any — and strip the rosemary needles off the woody stem.

name: Whipped Feta and Honey
tip: Block feta in brine, never the pre-crumbled kind — crumbles are coated in anti-caking starch and whip up chalky.

name: Blender Tzatziki
tip: Squeeze the grated cucumber in a tea towel first — skip it and you have soup by dinner.

name: Smoky Zucchini Tahini Dip
tip: Smoked paprika is doing the job the charred skin does in real baba ganoush — go heavier on it than feels right.

name: Herbed Labneh
tip: Labneh is thick enough to cavitate — add the lemon and oil first so there is something liquid at the blade.

name: Smoky Black Bean Dip
tip: Rinse canned beans until the water runs clear; the starchy packing liquid is what makes bean dips taste tinny.

name: Garden Mary
tip: A teaspoon of olive oil sounds odd in a tomato drink until you taste how it rounds the acid and carries the pepper.

name: Virgin Michelada
tip: Rim the glass with chili-lime seasoning and lime first, and spoon in a little olive brine with the olives — that is the salt.

name: Celery Salt Cooler
tip: The green apple is there for acid and body, not sweetness — a red apple makes this taste like a juice bar.

name: Pepino con Chile
tip: Stir the chia in after the blend and give it two minutes to swell — dropped in with everything else it welds itself to the blade.

name: Cold Miso Broth
tip: Miso clumps against cold broth, so blend it with a splash first and then pour the rest in.

name: Salted Cumin Lassi
tip: Toast the cumin in a dry pan for thirty seconds and crush it — ground straight from the jar it tastes like dust here.

name: Kimchi Tomato Sipper
tip: Use the kimchi brine from the bottom of the jar as part of the measure — that is where the sourness lives.

name: Gooseberry Frost
tip: Top and tail the gooseberries with your thumbnail first; the little stem ends are woody and they float.

name: Raspberry Rose Cloud
tip: Rose water goes from lovely to soapy fast; half a teaspoon is the whole point and a full one is a mistake.

name: Blueberry Thyme Field
tip: Strip the thyme leaves off the stem — the stems shred but never soften.

name: Acai and Toasted Coconut
tip: Toast the shredded coconut in a dry pan for a minute first — untoasted it just adds texture, toasted it adds flavour.

name: Rhubarb Fool
tip: Use raw rhubarb only if it is young and pink — older stalks need stewing and cooling first or the drink turns stringy.

name: Bramble Kefir
tip: Kefir thins out the longer it runs, so pulse it in short bursts rather than holding the button down.

name: Guanábana Cream
tip: Pick every black seed out of the soursop pulp before it goes near the blade — they are hard and bitter.

name: Lychee Drift
tip: Canned lychees work, but drain them and cut the syrup with extra lime or this gets cloying.

name: Piña con Tajín
tip: Rim the cup with a little extra chili-lime seasoning rather than adding more inside, or the whole drink turns salty.

name: Guava con Queso
tip: Let the cream cheese sit out ten minutes — straight from the fridge it leaves white specks that never blend.

name: Pink Pitaya Cloud
tip: Pitaya is all colour and very little flavour, so the banana is doing real work here — do not leave it out.

name: Coconut Lime Snow
tip: Zest the lime before you juice anything else that day — zest off a cut lime is a losing battle.

name: Mango Chamomile Cooler
tip: Brew the chamomile double strength and chill it — hot tea will melt the mango into slush before it blends.

name: Apricot Cardamom Cream
tip: A quarter teaspoon of cardamom is plenty — it is a spice that takes over a whole cup if you let it.

name: Nectarine Honeycomb
tip: Leave the nectarine skins on — they are thin and they give the drink a pink blush the flesh alone won't.

name: Sour Cherry Marzipan
tip: Almond extract is measured in drops for a reason — a quarter teaspoon reads as marzipan, a full one reads as soap.

name: Apricot Halva
tip: Soak the dried apricots in hot water for ten minutes and drain — dry ones just bounce around the blade.

name: Cherry Cacao Nib
tip: Add the nibs at the very end and pulse twice so they stay crunchy instead of turning to grit.

name: Watermelon Salt and Lime
tip: The pinch of salt is not optional — it is what makes watermelon taste like more of itself.

name: Melon Agua Fresca
tip: A cantaloupe that smells like nothing at the stem end will taste like nothing blended — check before you cut.

name: Honeydew Lime Frost
tip: Freeze the honeydew cubes overnight and you can skip half the ice, which keeps the flavour from washing out.

name: Melon and Labneh
tip: Labneh is thicker than yogurt, so start the blend with the water on top of it to get things moving.

name: Blood Orange Frost
tip: Segment the blood oranges rather than juicing them — the membranes are what make the colour muddy.

name: Tangerine Cream Cloud
tip: Peel the white pith off each segment; it is the difference between creamy and bitter.

name: Grapefruit Rosemary Chill
tip: Use only the soft top leaves of the rosemary sprig — woody stem never breaks down and you will find it later.

name: Clementine and Date
tip: Tear the dates open and check for pits even on bags marked pitted — one pit ends a blade assembly.

name: Lemon Poppy Seed
tip: Lemon curd does the work of juice and sugar together; add the zest last so it stays in flecks rather than dissolving.

name: Marmalade on Toast
tip: Let the oats sit in the oat milk for five minutes before blending — they thicken far better hydrated.

name: Elvis in a Cup
tip: Warm the peanut butter for ten seconds so it ribbons off the spoon instead of sitting in a lump on the blade.

name: Fig and Almond Butter
tip: Fresh figs blend to a beautiful jammy purple; dried ones need a soak first and taste far sweeter, so cut back on nothing else.

name: Banana Kulfi
tip: Blend the pistachios with the milk first so they break down, then add everything else — they are too hard to catch late.

name: Sesame Date Cream
tip: Use tahini from a fresh jar and stir it well — the separated oil at the top on its own makes the drink greasy.

name: Pistachio Orange Blossom
tip: Orange blossom water and rose water are not interchangeable here — blossom is the one that suits pistachio.

name: Coconut Butter Mango
tip: Coconut butter sets hard in the jar; stand it in warm water for a minute or it will never emulsify.

name: Minted Cucumber Kefir
tip: Scoop the watery seed core out of the cucumber; it dilutes the kefir and adds nothing.

name: Quark Berry Whip
tip: Quark curdles if you hit it with acid before fat, so let the milk and quark blend smooth before the berries go in.

name: Pineapple Cottage Whip
tip: Run the cottage cheese with the juice alone for fifteen seconds first or the curds survive the whole blend.

name: Ruby Kefir
tip: Cooked beet, never raw — raw beet stays gritty and tastes like soil in a cold drink.

name: Greek Honey Walnut
tip: Walnut skins turn bitter when over-blended, so stop as soon as the drink looks smooth.

name: Strawberry Kefir Swirl
tip: Stir the jam in by hand after blending if you want an actual swirl rather than a uniform pink.

name: Chocolate Orange Freeze
tip: Sift the cacao or shake it with the milk in a jar first — dry cocoa dumped on top clumps and floats.

name: Raspberry Truffle Blend
tip: Chop the chocolate fine before it goes in; a whole square just rattles and chips the ice instead.

name: Mexican Chocolate Banana
tip: The cayenne should be a warmth you notice on the third sip, not the first — start with less than you think.

name: White Chocolate Blackberry
tip: White chocolate seizes in cold liquid, so shave it thin rather than dropping in chunks.

name: Pear and Fennel Frost
tip: Use only the white bulb, not the fronds — fronds bring a licorice hit that swamps the pear.

name: Persimmon Maple Cream
tip: Only fully soft Hachiya persimmons work; an underripe one is astringent and will dry your mouth out.

name: Pumpkin Pear Spice
tip: Pure pumpkin puree, not pie filling — the filling is already sweetened and spiced and will double up on everything.

name: Butternut Orchard
tip: Roast and chill the squash rather than boiling it; boiled squash is watery and the drink goes thin.

name: Concord Freeze
tip: Frozen grapes are the whole trick — they blend to a sorbet texture no amount of ice will match.

name: Black Mission Fig and Walnut
tip: Snip the hard stem nub off each dried fig — it never softens and you will feel it in every sip.

name: Freezer Drawer Medley
tip: Whatever bags are nearly empty, roughly a cup and a quarter total — the lime is what stops random combinations tasting muddy.

name: Carrot Orange Frost
tip: Turmeric stains the gasket permanently — rinse the cup and the blade seal within a few minutes.

name: Jicama Lime Crush
tip: Peel jicama with a knife, not a peeler — the skin is thicker and tougher than it looks.

name: Maple Water Berry
tip: Add the chia after everything else is blended and let it stand two minutes, or it clumps around the blade.

name: Prickly Pear Cooler
tip: Wear a glove and scoop the flesh out with a spoon; the fine spines on the skin are the real hazard, not the seeds.

name: Everyday Banana Oat
tip: This is the plain Tuesday one — freeze peeled bananas in chunks on a tray so they do not fuse into a brick.

name: Avocado Lime Silk
tip: Avocado gives you silk without dairy, but it browns fast — blend it the minute you cut it open.

name: Namkeen Lassi
